name: UNC6692
description: UNC6692 conducts large-scale Microsoft Teams-based social engineering campaigns, posing as IT helpdesk personnel to manipulate employees into installing malware. Exploits the Teams External Access feature — enabled by default in many M365 tenants — to contact targets directly. Phishing alerts from collaboration tools now represent 42% of all alerts, up from 30%, as users have far lower suspicion of Teams messages vs. email.

ttps.notes: Microsoft Teams external access used to contact targets posing as IT helpdesk
Initial email flood campaign creates urgency before Teams contact
User prompted to install 'local patch' — actually malware payload
MFA code capture or OTP verification leads to account access
Prompts victim to approve MFA or provide OTP during social engineering call

malware_families: varies by campaign — typically RAT or infostealer payload
notable_techniques: Email flood pre-attack — overwhelms target with spam to create urgency and distraction
Teams tenant created with name like 'IT Helpdesk' or 'Technical Support' for credibility
Exploitation of Teams External Access — often enabled by default, rarely monitored
AI-assisted natural language generation for realistic conversation scripts
detection_opportunities: Teams messages from external tenants with helpdesk/IT-themed display names
Teams External Access enabled with no tenant allowlist restrictions
Email flood activity (hundreds of messages in short window) preceding Teams contact
New MFA device enrollment shortly after external Teams contact
Process execution of remote admin tools following Teams session
